newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies to vote on temporary labor bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies to vote on temporary labor bill.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies was due to vote later on Wednesday on a bill which would create a new, temporary labor contract which the government hopes will create more jobs, a deputy in charge of the bill said.

The Temporary Labor Contract would reduce the cost of hiring by between 20 and 25 percent by reducing employer contributions for temporary staff hired for a maximum of two years, Deputy Jose Mendonca Filho said.
Brazilian labor law currently does not distinguish between short-term and long-term hirings.
The bill, which had been due for a vote in the lower house on Tuesday, includes safeguards to stop employers from firing existing staff and replacing them with new, short-term workers.
It also sets proportional limits on the total number of employees companies may hire under the new contract.
About 30 million Brazilians work in the "informal sector," an unofficially registered area of the economy in which workers lack contracts and do not remit payroll taxes.
The government floated the idea of the temporary contract earlier this year but the bill was considered too sensitive for approval before October and November's municipal elections.
